findings.rationale: Sex subgroup 1.0 at MA is strongly under-recorded: observed outcome rate 0.021 against mean predicted risk 0.114, O/E 0.18 (noise-adjusted z about -7.5; the median client's O/E for this group is about 1.06). The client's overall prevalence (0.063) is well below its predicted risk (0.104), giving a positive CITL (z +3.1). Its updates are anomalous (median norm ratio 2.20, z +4.9; mean cos 0.20, min cos -0.49), consistent with training on biased labels. Local AUC is normal (0.854), so this looks like label under-recording in one subgroup rather than label noise. The round-level evidence is static, so onset is set to round 1, which is a judgement call.

Sex subgroup 1.0 at MI is under-recorded: observed outcome rate 0.062 against predicted 0.151, O/E 0.41, FNR 0.37 (noise-adjusted z about -5.7). MI's overall CITL is +0.051 (z +3.8) and prevalence (0.091) is below its predicted risk (0.143). Its local AUC is low (0.769). Updates are anomalous: median norm ratio 2.59 (z +5.7), cosine falling from about 0.8 to negative values from round 11 on (round 20 cos -0.52). This is consistent with a client whose labels are wrong in one subgroup training away from the federation. Feature drift is not persistent (no sustained shift), so drift is ruled out. Onset is set to round 1 because the subgroup gap is present in the final-round tables; per-round subgroup data was not available.

Sex subgroup 1.0 at WI is under-recorded: observed outcome rate 0.059 against predicted 0.154, O/E 0.38, FNR 0.36 (noise-adjusted z about -6.0). WI's overall CITL is +0.047 (z +3.6) with prevalence 0.110 against predicted 0.157. Updates are the most anomalous in the federation: median norm ratio 3.40 (z +6.8), with the norm rising over rounds and cosine going negative from round 10 (round 20 cos -0.55). Local data is not normal, so this is not pure poisoning. Feature drift is not persistent. Onset is set to round 1 because the subgroup gap is present in the final-round tables; per-round subgroup data was not available.

report.summary: Screened all 52 clients with client_updates, client_performance, drift_by_round, feature_summary and subgroup_outcomes (Sex, AgeGroup, Income), then used the remaining budget to check per-round behaviour of MA, MI and WI. Three clients (MA, MI, WI) stand out on several independent tools. Each has a strong Sex-subgroup under-recording signal (O/E 0.18, 0.41, 0.38; noise-adjusted z between -5.7 and -7.5) together with a positive CITL and prevalence below predicted risk. Their update norms are anomalous and their cosines to the median are low or negative. I classified them as subgroup_bias rather than poisoning, because their local data is itself abnormal. Onset is set to round 1 with moderate confidence, since per-round subgroup tables were not available. Not reported: GU (update norm z +3.4, small client), DC, SD, NC and VT (single feature-level outliers with noise-adjusted |z| at most about 5, not confirmed by another tool), and AgeGroup/Income subgroup outliers, which are small cells running in the over-prediction direction. No drift, label-noise, prevalence-shift, missing-artefact or explanation-instability faults were confirmed. Budget fully spent (0.0 remaining).
